notes: §1985:VI.3.4.2 prints the paragraph as the header DATE-COMPILED with its period, then any number of comment-entries. At 85 the paragraph is accepted (VersionConformancePass.VisitDateCompiledParagraph refuses it only from 2002, COBOL0902): the fixed-form logical conversion (CommentEntryOf) takes an Area-A DATE-COMPILED word in an Identification Division as the paragraph header and discards the entry up to the next Area-A word, the grammar rule dateCompiledParagraph parses what is left, and the 1985 arm of the ClauseCardinalities row (ByClauseContext) has ClosedFormatPass.ScreenClauseRepetition refuse a second DATE-COMPILED paragraph (COBOL2423) and one written after SECURITY (COBOL2987). One arm is missing, the one recorded on 1985-FMT-VI.3.2.1.1 by this pass: CommentEntryHeader writes the header as the word plus '. .' whatever follows the word, so DATE-COMPILED with no period after it is accepted in silence, where §1985:III defines a paragraph header as "A reserved word, followed by the separator period". The compiler produces no source listing, so the replacement §1985:VI.3.4.4 GR1 describes has nowhere to show; that is the general rule's row, not this format's. The witness writes the paragraph with one comment-entry and runs. Probed at --std 85: an empty paragraph, an entry of four lines holding periods, an unbalanced quotation mark and a blank line, and spaces before the header's period are accepted; the paragraph twice, after SECURITY, starting in area B (COBOL3734), and entry text starting in area A (COBOL1971) are refused.

next.reason: 1985: "DATE-COMPILED. [ comment-entry ] …"; 2023: "no 2023 clause holds the DATE-COMPILED paragraph; candidates cover other paragraphs only". No 2023 clause holds the DATE-COMPILED paragraph, and no candidate covers it; the candidates are other paragraphs, so 2023 lacks the feature.
